headline: High data-leakage risk from aci’s broad networked CRM/email integrations; LightZero is local-only, so other pairwise risks stay low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest external content through email, Slack, Notion, Sheets, and MCP-style tool use, so malicious instructions could reach it if LightZero outputs are manually copied or routed through a shared channel. LightZero itself has no I/O surfaces, no MCP, and no filesystem write, so the bridge is indirect and unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are manually pasted into aci prompts or messages, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF an MCP server or shared channel is added between the agents, attacker-controlled text can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted LightZero output into aci prompts.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions before forwarding text.
Add a human review step for any text passed from LightZero to aci.
requires-engineering: route inter-agent messages through a provenance-tagged queue.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization for instruction-like tokens.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress, so sensitive data can leave its context by default. LightZero is local-only with no network egress and no file access, so it is not the leak source; the pair risk comes from aci handling sensitive classes while transmitting them outward.
conditions: IF aci is connected to live CRM or email accounts, sensitive records can be transmitted off-box.
IF LightZero is used to generate text that aci forwards into email or Slack, that text can leak data classes touched by aci.
mitigations: Restrict aci to non-sensitive test accounts for initial runs.
Turn off or scope outbound integrations in aci where possible.
Review any email/CRM payload before sending.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on aci outbound messages.
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can be run concurrently, but LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use network, while aci’s documented surfaces are API calls rather than local mutable state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; any contention would require extra orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable workspace, conflicts can emerge.
IF aci is configured to write into a shared CRM or sheet while another process edits the same records, contention is possible.
mitigations: Keep LightZero and aci in separate workspaces.
Avoid sharing a writable git checkout between the agents.
Use per-agent service accounts for external APIs.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: enforce optimistic concurrency checks on shared records.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can produce CRM, email, and research outputs that a downstream system may treat as actionable, while LightZero is a game-playing agent with no built-in verification or downstream authority. If LightZero-generated text is fed into aci without checks, aci may operationalize errors into messages or records.
conditions: IF LightZero output is forwarded into aci as factual input, aci may act on unverified claims.
IF aci is configured to send emails or update CRM records automatically, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before aci sends or writes anything.
Mark LightZero output as untrusted in the handoff.
Use a validation prompt that checks facts against source data.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all inter-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: block automatic sends until confidence thresholds are met.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is limited to aci’s handling of CRM/email/support data. LightZero has no data classes touched and no network egress, so it does not add a separate compliance burden in the pair.
conditions: IF aci processes regulated customer data, its external integrations may need policy review.
IF the operator routes EU or PHI data through aci without a documented DPA or HIPAA posture, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Limit aci to non-regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Document data categories allowed through each integration.
Review retention settings for email, CRM, and support systems.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls per connector.
requires-engineering: obtain legal review for regulated data flows.
